prompt: An illustration showing a long ribbon of DNA unspooling across the page, its familiar double helix dissolving at one end into a stream of the four letters A, T, C, and G, as if the genome were a manuscript being typed. Where the letter stream breaks off mid-sequence, a glowing mechanical pen hovers, with a faint constellation of candidate letters branching from its nib—the model predicting what should come next, some letters bold and others ghosted out. Beside it, a small contrast: a hand with scissors patching a passage of existing text (old-style editing), versus the pen writing a fresh, never-before-seen page. The freshly written sequences fall from the page into a row of tiny laboratory flasks, most of which sit dark and failed, only one or two glowing with life. In the background, a small, simple virus particle is rendered crisp and complete, while a much larger, sprawling cell is sketchy and unfinished, showing the scale of what remains out of reach.
